instructions: Take the steak out of the fridge, pat it dry, and sprinkle 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper over both sides.
In a small bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of the olive oil with the balsamic vinegar, 1 minced garlic clove, honey, Dijon, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a heavy 12 inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.

Add the steak and cook for 4 minutes without moving it, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan. Flip it and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. You're cooking it to 130°F in the middle for medium-rare, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Press the center: it should feel springy, like the base of your thumb.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the tomatoes and thinly slice half the red onion. Divide the greens among 4 plates and top with the tomatoes and onion.
Slice the steak thinly across the grain and lay it over the salads.
Sprinkle the blue cheese on top and drizzle each salad with half of the dressing.
Serve with the rest of the dressing on the side.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Cup of Yum (5.0 from 22 ratings) tosses sliced steak, tomato, red onion and blue cheese over greens with a balsamic, honey and Dijon dressing, half on the salad and half on the side. It gives no steak method and only 8 oz of steak for 6, so this uses 1 lb of sirloin for 4 and the sear is Pomona's own: a hot skillet, 4 minutes without moving it, then a rest. Amy Casey Cooks and Slow the Cook Down also sear and rest the steak, with only a handful of ratings. About 20 minutes in all.
